findings.evidence: Light of wavelength λ is incident normally on two narrow slits S₁ and S₂, a small distance apart. Bright and dark fringes are observed on a screen a long distance away from the slits.
findings.suggested: Remove this double-slit fringe question from the stationary-waves chapter.
findings.resolution: fix: The finding is valid: this tests the path difference for double-slit dark fringes, belonging to 9702-8.3.3, beyond the 8.1 bundle objectives. The source image confirms C: destructive interference occurs at positive path differences lambda/2, 3lambda/2, ... so S2P - S1P = (n - 1/2)lambda. The tagged bank has answer C and no examiner comment. Do not mark it off syllabus globally. Overrides are applied after bank selection, so an override alone cannot remove it from this chapter. Under qid 9702_w21_11_q28 in build/work/mcq/overrides.json set kcs=["9702-8.3.3"], stem="Light of wavelength λ is incident normally on two narrow slits S₁ and S₂, a small distance apart. Bright and dark fringes are observed on a screen a long distance away from the slits, as shown in the diagram. The nth dark fringe from the central bright fringe is observed at point P on the screen. Which equation is correct for all positive values of n?", options={"A":"S₂P − S₁P = nλ/2","B":"S₂P − S₁P = nλ","C":"S₂P − S₁P = (n − 1/2)λ","D":"S₂P − S₁P = (n + 1/2)λ"}, answer="C", explanation="Normal incidence makes the light at the two slits in phase. Dark fringes occur at odd half-wavelength path differences. Counting from n = 1 gives S₂P − S₁P = (n − 1/2)λ, so C is correct. A also includes bright fringes for even n; B describes bright fringes; D starts at the second dark fringe." Preserve the source image.
